User: the way I understand it, apps should be able to create their own kind builders, so I could have an app that makes up its own kind schema

Assistant: Yes — that's exactly the intended design, and it's worth saying it's a *first-class extension point*, not a workaround. The owner's own framing on NIP-29 is the cleanest statement of the principle: *"chat is just one more event kind — this is poor design"* was the complaint that drove NIP-29 to a single generic `nmp.nip29.publish` with the consumer declaring kinds. Kinds aren't special to the framework. So an app inventing kind 232123 with its own tag schema is the same shape as anything else. [...] User: publish a gh issue to explore this question and design space, make it clear that the intent goal is what I stated -- an app should easily be able to define its made up kind with its schema builder and whatnot and should be a first-class citizen. Don't add your commentary on how to do this [...] - **App-defined kinds — now a live v1 workstream.** Notably, the #2408 I filed this session already got decomposed: `#2413` (app-local schema/builder drift gates), `#2414` (prove app-private kind in starter DX) — and they're labeled **`phase:v1-dx`**, meaning this got pulled *into* v1 DX, not deferred. That's the agent activity, and it's a real scope addition since my last "done" report. [...] 3. **App-defined kinds first-class** (#2408/#2413/#2414) — external apps have their own kinds; this is now v1-dx, and it's at ~10%.
